request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027.
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity under a preliminary board, publish technical transition architecture and migration plan, and launch a public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under published rules in Q4 2026, with the elected board assuming its mandate.
Serve all public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod from the new stack in Q1 2027, transfer Blockfrost IP to the governing entity, and maintain current service performance through cutover.
Open a public sustainability consultation in Q2-Q3 2027 and publish a proposal and documented outcome for the chosen long-term direction.
Operate the public API through 2027 at a minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA and publish quarterly reports covering technical metrics and budget summary.
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition under governance involving Intersect and CDH contract administration; final not-for-profit entity not yet stated.
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed public API operated under an independent not-for-profit or host organization, with 18 months of transition and operations funding.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own infrastructure or node.
The proposal states Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem surveys show Blockfrost hosted-platform usage grew from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal states Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal states more than 50% of all Cardano transactions are submitted through Blockfrost in most epochs.
The proposal states more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the decentralized Blockfrost operator effort.
The proposal states 90% of Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier and that the commercial model has been difficult for financing that public-good operation.
The proposal commits to transferring Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing not-for-profit entity during the transition.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, valued at 1,868,266 USD using 0.19 USD per ADA, for 18 months of staffing, operations and infrastructure, and legal/accounting costs.
The proposal states any unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

The proposal states a written off-chain legal contract between Input Output and Cardano Development Holdings will define delivery schedule, dispute resolution, milestone acceptance, and third-party assurance.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to fund Blockfrost's 18-month transition from a commercial service into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, citing strong developer adoption and transaction-submission dependence, but many operational, usage, risk, and sustainability assertions are asserted rather than evidenced inside the anchor.
